resources.string: Renal tubules from corpuscle to collecting duct
Tubule segments
Urinary pole
At this opening, filtrate in Bowman\'s space enters the proximal tubule. The glomerulus is the capillary tuft inside the corpuscle, not part of the tubule.
Loop of Henle bend
The thin descending limb turns back toward the cortex at this hairpin in the medulla. The length of the loop varies among nephrons.
Thick ascending limb
The wider returning limb rises from the medulla to the cortex, passes close to the vascular pole of its own corpuscle, and leads into the distal convoluted tubule.
Distal tubule at the corpuscle and collecting junction
Distal junctions
Macula densa
This patch of tightly packed cells sits near the end of the thick ascending limb beside the vascular pole of the glomerulus. It lies just upstream of the distal convoluted tubule.
Distal convolution
This coiled segment stays in the cortex. Its lumen is continuous with the ascending limb, not with the nearby glomerular capillaries.
Cuboidal lining
A single layer of cuboidal epithelial cells surrounds the distal tubule lumen. These cells lack the dense brush border of the proximal tubule, so the lumen has a clearer edge.
Connecting tubule
This short segment carries fluid from the distal convolution into the collecting system. The collecting duct also receives fluid from other nephrons.
Collecting ducts from cortex to papilla
Collecting path
Cortical collecting duct
Connecting tubules from different nephrons feed the same cortical collecting duct. Two separate nephron outlets join the shared path shown here.
Medullary collecting duct
Collecting ducts descend through the renal pyramid. In the inner medulla they converge into larger channels as they approach the papilla.
Papillary duct
A papillary duct, also called a duct of Bellini, is the final collecting channel. It opens at the tip of the papilla into a minor calyx; one outlet is shown here.
Minor calyx
This cup surrounds the papilla and receives urine from its openings. It belongs to the drainage passages beyond the collecting ducts.
